name: Genmaicha

origin.regionNote: nationwide — a style, not a garden
origin.subregion: bancha or sencha blended with popped rice

pluckStandard: green tea blended with roasted popped rice

transformation.note: The leaf is still a green tea; toasted rice and a medium fire colour the cup.

processing.description: Toasted and popped rice (not genmai porridge) mixed into bancha or sencha; some lots include matcha.

gongfu.curveException: Japanese greens go long–short–long: the first cool steep needs time, the second is quick because the leaf is open, the third lengthens again.

water.note: 80–85 °C. Rice can go starchy if boiled hard for ages.

storage: Airtight; rice oils stale. Finish opened bags promptly.

shelfLife.window: within a year of roast or packing

qualityMarkers.claim: optional matcha dust vivid not brown

summary: Green tea cut with popped toasted rice: popcorn comfort, still a Japanese green.
